about: Landmark and building descriptors for the Atlanta bake (map/city.json): what a building looks like beyond its OSM footprint. Tier A: iconic buildings, facts read from the sources listed; Tier B: further named buildings with a lighter descriptor that is mostly deduced. In every entry "notes" ends with "deduced: ..." naming the fields that were NOT read from a source; in Tier B the descriptive sentence is from memory unless its fact is named as read. Lengths are metres; height is the architectural top, roofHeight where the crown starts (height = roofHeight + crown.height; an "antenna" crown is a mast that stands ABOVE height). massing.setbacks[].at is a fraction of the height and inset a fraction of the plan width; massing.taper > 0 means wider at the base, < 0 an overhanging top. Colours are best guesses for the cladding and glass in daylight.

frame.note: match.at is [lon, lat] (WGS84), a point inside the footprint of the main mass in the bake; match.xz is the same point in bake-frame metres (x east, z south of center), as city.json before MapWorld shifts it to the spawn.

buildings.name: Bank of America Plaza
buildings.architect: Kevin Roche John Dinkeloo and Associates
buildings.notes: The "pencil building", tallest in Georgia. Postmodern, Art Deco in feeling: a dark shaft with strong vertical lines and notched corners, square in plan and turned 45 degrees to Peachtree Street, set back from the street behind lawns and granite stairs. The inhabited shaft ends in a flat roof; above it stands an open-lattice pyramid of gilded steel girders (its top is the 933 ft / 284 m "roof" of the infobox), then a 90 ft (27 m) obelisk spire covered in 23-karat gold leaf. At night the lattice glows yellow-orange (high-pressure sodium). The engine should draw the crown as an OPEN lattice pyramid with the obelisk on top, not a solid pyramid. deduced: roofHeight (55 floors; the page only says the shaft ends in a flat roof), crown.height (311.8 - 240: about 44 m of lattice pyramid + the 27 m obelisk), massing (plan and rotation from the OSM footprint and photos), facade.color (the page says only "dark color"; red-brown granite from memory), facade.glass, glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.litFraction.

buildings.name: Truist Plaza
buildings.notes: Formerly One Peachtree Center / SunTrust Plaza; second tallest in Atlanta. Postmodern square tower "with an elaborate base and crown" (Wikipedia), its corners notched so the plan reads as a stepped cross; a rotating light at the top; an antenna brings it to 274.9 m. OSM models it as 104 building:parts with levels but no heights, so the bake tops out at 193 m (60 levels x 3.2 m): scale the pieces to height. Truist announced crown signage in 2021. deduced: roofHeight and crown.height (the stepped tiers of the crown are about the top 30 m), massing.podium and setbacks, facade.material and color (grey granite piers with grey-blue reflective glass, from memory of photos), glass, glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown.material and lit colour (white), ground, night.sign (assumed installed as announced), litFraction.

buildings.name: 191 Peachtree Tower
buildings.notes: Postmodern tower by Philip Johnson and John Burgee: two conjoined shafts with a deep recess between them, each topped by its own open, columned crown (a classical pavilion); the lit double crown is the building's signature at night. Flame-finished Rosa Dante granite and grey tinted glass. The entrance on Peachtree Street is a seven-storey, 102 ft (31 m) atrium. In the bake the tower is three parts of 234.7 m (the two shafts and the link): the recess and the crowns are not modelled. deduced: roofHeight and crown.height (the crowns are about six storeys), crown.type is the nearest enum value for two open colonnaded pavilions, massing.plan, facade.color (hex for pink-beige Rosa Dante granite), glass hex, glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown.lit colour (warm white), night.litFraction.

buildings.name: Westin Peachtree Plaza Hotel
buildings.notes: A 73-storey cylinder of dark reflective glass, the tallest hotel in the world when it opened; more floors than any other building in Georgia. A glass elevator tube runs up the outside of the cylinder; the top floors hold the revolving Sun Dial restaurant; antenna to 269.1 m. The cylinder in the bake is the OSM building:part (1246 m2, about 40 m across, tagged building:material=glass, 220.4 m); with --keep-outlines the block-sized podium outline is kept under it at a default 27 m. Wikipedia gives a "187 ft (57 m) diameter", which does not fit the mapped cylinder (probably the base). deduced: roofHeight and crown (the restaurant floors read as a cap), massing.podium floors, facade.color and glass (bronze mirror glass, from memory), glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight (220.4 / 73), ground, night.sign, crownLight, litFraction.

buildings.name: Georgia-Pacific Tower
buildings.notes: Georgia-Pacific Center, 133 Peachtree Street: "a stair-like design that staggers down to the ground", clad in pink granite quarried at Marble Falls, Texas. The stair is on ONE side only (the plan shortens in steps as the tower rises); OSM models it as four parts of 100, 150, 200 and 212 m, which the bake carries, with building:material=granite and building:colour=#ba9287. The Wikipedia list gives 51 floors, the article 52. deduced: massing.setbacks (fractions from the OSM part heights and areas; one-sided), facade.system (flush square windows in a granite grid, from memory), glass hex, glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.litFraction.

buildings.name: Tower Square
buildings.notes: Formerly the Southern Bell / BellSouth Center and AT&T Midtown Center I, in Midtown at the north edge of the bake. A pale slab with close-set vertical piers and dark window strips, flat top. OSM tags building:material=concrete, roof:shape=flat. The infobox says completed 1980, the text 1982. Vacant from 2020 until a first tenant signed in 2026, so few windows are lit. deduced: archetype, massing.plan, facade (pale precast or stone piers with dark glass, from memory of photos; the sources give only "concrete"), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.litFraction.

buildings.name: State of Georgia Building
buildings.notes: 2 Peachtree Street at Five Points, built as the First National Bank Building: the tallest building in the Southeast in 1966, now state offices. International style slab with white vertical piers and dark glass; an antenna reaches 182.6 m. deduced: archetype, massing.plan, facade.material and color (white marble piers, from memory), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown (the antenna mast: 182.6 - 169.5 m), ground, night.litFraction.

buildings.name: Atlanta Marriott Marquis
buildings.notes: The "pregnant building": a narrow concrete slab whose long sides bulge outward toward the base (from the side it is said to look like a Coca-Cola bottle), around an atrium 143 m high that was the largest in the world in 1985. Brutalist / neo-futurist. The article gives 47 storeys, the Wikipedia list 52. In the bake the slab is a part named "Marriott" (168.9 m) on a 3-level podium named "Atlanta Marriott Marquis". taper here means the plan is WIDER at the base: the lower third flares out along the long sides. deduced: massing.taper, facade (pale concrete with horizontal window bands, from memory), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.sign (red Marriott lettering at the top), litFraction.

buildings.name: 101 Marietta Street (Centennial Tower)
buildings.notes: Modernist office tower of 1975 beside Centennial Olympic Park; the 1998 renovation gave it a new facade and the chevrons at the top, which raised it from 136 m to 140 m. OSM tags height=164, so the bake is 24 m too tall. deduced: massing.plan, facade (blue-green reflective glass after the 1998 recladding, from memory), glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown (one chevron, an inverted V, on each face; "flat" plus 4 m is the nearest enum value), crown.lit, ground, night.

buildings.name: Equitable Building (100 Peachtree)
buildings.notes: International style black box on a plaza across from Woodruff Park: "the tower's black finish stood in sharp contrast to the surrounding buildings". The EQUITABLE sign at the top was a skyline fixture; since 2017 a digital LED display there shows the logo of Georgia's Own Credit Union. Floors: 32 in the article, 34 in the Wikipedia list, 35 in OSM. deduced: massing.plan, facade (black metal mullions and dark glass in the Miesian manner), glass, glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.sign text and colours, litFraction.

buildings.name: Georgia State Capitol
buildings.notes: The Gold Dome. Renaissance Revival / Neoclassical, modelled on the U.S. Capitol: a four-storey portico with a stone pediment on six Corinthian columns, a central rotunda between two wings, 106 m north to south. The dome (23 m in diameter) has been gilded with gold leaf from Dahlonega since 1958 and carries the statue Miss Freedom. OSM gives the body 4 levels (13.8 m in the bake, kept by --keep-outlines) and one 303 m2 part tagged roof:shape=dome with no height (23.4 m in the bake): the drum, dome, lantern and statue need their own geometry. deduced: height (the 272 ft 4.5 in usually quoted to the top of the statue; the article lists that figure without a clear label), roofHeight (cornice of the body), crown.height, facade.material (Indiana limestone, from memory) and color, glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.

buildings.name: Atlanta City Hall
buildings.notes: Neo-Gothic high-rise city hall of 1930 on Mitchell Street, a slender tower on a wide base, like many American city halls of its time; a modern annex of 1989 lies behind it. In the bake: "City Hall Tower" (66.6 m, the OSM height) and two lower "Atlanta City Hall" parts (the annex). deduced: floors (about 14; OSM says 17 levels), roofHeight, massing, facade.material and color (cream terra cotta; the enum has no terra cotta, limestone is the nearest), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown, ground, night.

buildings.name: Mercedes-Benz Stadium
buildings.architect: HOK (360 Architecture); tvsdesign; Goode Van Slyke; Stanley Beaman & Sears
buildings.notes: Home of the Falcons and Atlanta United, 71,000 seats. The signature is the retractable "pinwheel" roof of eight translucent triangular panels around a circular opening inspired by the Pantheon; below its rim the "Halo" video board. Much of the exterior is clear polymer or glass; the body is angular, in large triangular facets. OSM tags height=93. The 12 m steel falcon sculpture stands outside. deduced: the faceted body, facade.material and color (silver metal facets between the glazed areas), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown ("flat" is the nearest value for the petal roof; the Mercedes star is painted on it), crown.lit and night.crownLight (red on Falcons nights), ground, night.sign, litFraction.

buildings.name: State Farm Arena
buildings.notes: Home of the Atlanta Hawks (opened 1999 as Philips Arena, renovated 2017-18). On the side facing downtown, the angled steel columns that carry the roof spell out "ATLANTA" in letters several storeys high: that is the feature to reproduce. OSM has no height or levels, so the bake height (33.5 m) is the baker's default. deduced: height, facade, glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.

buildings.name: Georgia Aquarium
buildings.notes: The largest aquarium in the United States, at the north end of Centennial Olympic Park (Pemberton Place). "It has a blue metal-and-glass exterior"; the entrance front rises like the bow of a ship. OSM has the outline with 5 levels (17 m in the bake, kept by --keep-outlines) and one roof part coloured "blue". deduced: height (about 30 m), archetype (nearest value for a large hall), facade hex values, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown, ground, night.

buildings.name: World of Coca-Cola
buildings.notes: The Coca-Cola museum at Pemberton Place, opened May 24, 2007 (it replaced the 1990 pavilion at Underground Atlanta); two floors. A low pavilion with a tall glazed entrance holding a giant Coca-Cola bottle, and the red Coca-Cola disc sign. OSM has no height or levels (26.4 m in the bake is the baker's default). deduced: height, archetype (nearest value for a low pavilion), facade, glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.

buildings.name: SkyView Atlanta
buildings.notes: A 200 ft (61 m) transportable Ferris wheel with 42 air-conditioned gondolas, across Centennial Olympic Park Drive from the park (it stood in Paris and Pensacola before). NOT a building: the OSM footprint is a 114 m2 strip under the wheel tagged height=61, min_height=5, roof:shape=round, which the bake extrudes as a 61 m slab. The engine should replace it with a wheel (white steel rim and spokes, A-frame legs, gondolas), standing in the vertical plane through the long axis of the footprint; the rim is lit at night in changing colours. The footprint's long side is 50 m and runs 41 degrees east of north (bake frame): the wheel's plane. deduced: year (2013, from memory; the page gives no date in the passage read), wheel colours, night.

buildings.name: The Center (CNN Center)
buildings.notes: Opened in 1976 as the Omni International complex, CNN Center from 1987 to 2024, now being renovated as "The Center" (stylised The CTR, its name in OSM and the bake): office blocks around a large skylit atrium, with the Omni hotel attached on the north side. The big red CNN logo that stood at the entrance has gone with CNN. OSM gives 15 levels and no height (49 m in the bake). deduced: floors (14 office storeys), height, archetype, facade (pale precast bands with ribbon windows, from memory), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.

buildings.name: Hyatt Regency Atlanta
buildings.notes: John Portman's 1967 Regency Hyatt House, whose 22-storey atrium changed hotel design. On the roof the revolving restaurant Polaris sits "just beneath the blue dome-shaped structure which gives the hotel its distinctive profile": a blue saucer dome on a stalk. Two extensions: the cylindrical, mirror-glass Radius Tower (1971, formerly Ivy Tower, the stand-in for the Westin in the film Sharky's Machine) and the International Tower (1982). In the bake the parts are named "Atrium" (100 m), "International Tower" (100 m), "Radius Tower" (98 m), and "Hyatt Regency Atlanta" (the dome part at 104 m and the 2-level podium): those part heights are too high for the atrium block, which is 22 storeys (about 70-82 m) with the dome reaching 103.6 m. deduced: roofHeight and crown.height, crown.material (the blue dome is glazed; the enum has no such value), massing, facade (concrete with stacked balcony bands), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.

buildings.name: Flatiron Building (English-American Building)
buildings.notes: Atlanta's oldest standing skyscraper (1897, five years before New York's Flatiron), on the wedge between Peachtree, Poplar and Broad Streets; Neo-Classical / Neo-Renaissance, 11 storeys, "c. 50 m" (OSM says 44 m). Named FlatironCity in OSM and the bake. deduced: roofHeight, archetype, facade.material and color (buff brick over a stone base, with bay windows on the long sides, from memory), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown (a projecting cornice), ground, night.

buildings.name: Candler Building
buildings.notes: Built in 1906 by the Coca-Cola magnate Asa Candler, then the tallest in the city: 17 storeys, about 240 ft, Beaux-Arts / Neo-Renaissance, on the north edge of Woodruff Park; now The Candler Hotel. OSM tags height=73.2. deduced: roofHeight, archetype, facade.material and color (white Georgia marble with carved ornament, from memory; not in the passage read), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown (heavy cornice), ground, night.

buildings.name: Healey Building
buildings.notes: Gothic Revival office tower of 1913-14 in Fairlie-Poplar, 16 storeys, the last big skyscraper of the pre-war boom; planned as twin towers joined by an atrium, only the west one was built. Condominiums above shops and galleries since 2001. OSM tags height=62.7. deduced: roofHeight, archetype, facade.material and color (pale terra cotta piers; limestone is the nearest enum value), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown (Gothic parapet), ground, night.

buildings.name: Fox Theatre
buildings.architect: Marye, Alger and Vinour (Olivier J. Vinour)
buildings.notes: The "Fabulous Fox", a 4,665-seat movie palace of 1929 planned as the Yaarab Shrine Temple: the exterior is Islamic / Moorish, with onion domes, minarets and horseshoe arches; a long entrance arcade on Peachtree Street under the marquee and the vertical FOX sign. Midtown, at the north edge of the bake. OSM has ten parts, one tagged roof:shape=onion and one dome; the bake heights (up to 23.4 m) come from levels. deduced: the onion domes, minarets and arches (the OSM roof shapes and memory; the article says only Moorish / Islamic), the arcade and the FOX sign, floors, height (to the top of the onion dome), roofHeight, archetype (nearest value; "Moorish" has none), facade.material and color (cream and buff brick in bands), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown.material and height, ground, night.

buildings.name: Georgian Terrace Hotel
buildings.architect: William Lee Stoddart; Smallwood, Reynolds, Stewart, Stewart (1991 wing)
buildings.notes: Beaux-Arts hotel of 1911 across Peachtree Street from the Fox, "built of butter-colored brick, marble, and limestone" to evoke Paris: turreted corners, Palladian windows, wrap-around columned terraces, a two-storey window arcade and a terracotta cornice. The original block has 10 storeys; a 19-storey wing was added in 1991. OSM models 15 parts (65 m for the wing, 33-36 m for the 1911 block) with building:material=limestone;marble;brick and building:colour=#b1a5a2, which the bake carries. podium here stands for the 10-storey 1911 block in front of the wing. deduced: roofHeight, archetype, facade.color (hex for butter-coloured brick; OSM's colour is greyer), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown, ground, night.

buildings.name: One Coca-Cola Plaza
buildings.notes: The headquarters tower of The Coca-Cola Company on North Avenue, on the western skyline of the bake: "the company's 29-story headquarters building in Atlanta, known as One Coca-Cola Plaza, was designed by FABRAP and completed in 1980". The Coca-Cola script is at the top of the tower. deduced: archetype, massing.plan, facade (pale precast with vertical ribs and dark windows, from memory), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.sign colour, litFraction.

buildings.name: Hurt Building
buildings.notes: Triangular office building at 50 Hurt Plaza, built 1913-1926 (first home of the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta), in the Chicago School manner: "uninterrupted marble and glazed brick piers with ornamental terra cotta spandrels terminating in a heavy decorative cornice". 17 or 18 storeys depending on the passage. OSM tags height=82 (high for 18 storeys; kept as the only figure found). deduced: roofHeight, archetype, facade.color, glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown height, ground (a domed entrance rotunda at the apex), night.

buildings.name: Peachtree Summit
buildings.notes: A 30-storey triangle on the lot between the Downtown Connector, West Peachtree Street and Ivan Allen Jr. Boulevard, over the Civic Center MARTA station, with a three-storey lobby: the tower you pass closest to on the Connector. Federal offices. OSM tags building:material=concrete and height=125 on the outline, but the bake pieces are two parts of 97 m (30 levels): scale to height. The Wikipedia list gives 123.8 m and 31 floors. deduced: archetype, facade (concrete with horizontal window bands, from memory), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, night.

buildings.name: Georgia Power Company Corporate Headquarters
buildings.notes: Passive solar design of 1981 beside the Connector at Ralph McGill Boulevard: on the south face each floor extends 15 in (380 mm) beyond the one below, so the face leans outward as it rises and shades the windows beneath in summer. taper is negative here to say the south face overhangs (the top is deeper than the base). Heights disagree: the article says 24 storeys and 91 m, the Wikipedia list 101.2 m, and the OSM part (so the bake) 121.5 m. deduced: archetype, massing, facade (bands of dark glass and metal), glass, glassReflect, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.sign, litFraction.

buildings.name: Sam Nunn Atlanta Federal Center
buildings.notes: The largest federal building in the Southeast: a U-shaped complex of a 24-storey tower (387 ft), an 11-storey mid-rise, the 1924 main building of Rich's department store, and an eight-storey bridge six storeys above Forsyth Street. The bake has seven parts (118.3 m tower, two 36 m blocks, the raised bridge, the Rich's store). deduced: archetype, facade (buff precast and stone with punched windows), glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, crown, ground, night.

buildings.name: Atlanta Central Library
buildings.notes: Marcel Breuer's last completed building (1980): an eight-storey Brutalist block that fills its city block at Margaret Mitchell Square, "a concrete facade with an inverted general shape and some windows": the upper floors step outward over the lower ones. taper is negative to say the top overhangs. Renovated 2018-2021, when more windows were cut in. OSM gives 6 levels (20.2 m in the bake). deduced: height (8 storeys), facade hex and panel module, glass, vertical, bay, floorHeight, ground, night.
